messages:
elena: FYI hitting duplicate model outputs from the python async client when a streaming request times out and the client retries. Repro in sample app attached. Looks like idempotency-key gets lost for the retry and the previous stream isn't aborted, so consumers see two full responses.

sam: Ugh. Is this the streaming API (`.stream`) or the normal generate call?

elena: streaming `.chat.stream(...)` with an idempotency_key set. Sequence: send request -> server 504 (gateway timeout) -> client retry kicks in -> second attempt succeeds -> both stream iterators get results and both delivered to app. Client v0.7.3.

kevin: Do you have logs and a minimal repro? Might be similar to the deadline-propagation bug we patched, where the retry wrapper didn't cancel the original iterator.

elena: pasted a tiny repro below and a log snippet. Reproducer uses asyncio and yields tokens from the returned async iterator.

elena: ```python
# simplified repro
async def call_stream(client):
    async for chunk in client.chat.stream(model="redwood-small", messages=[...], idempotency_key="abc-123", timeout=10):
        process(chunk)

# start the call, simulate a server 504 then a success on retry
```

elena: logs: 
```
2026-02-15T12:04:05Z elena INFO request id=abc-123 attempt=1 -> 504 Gateway Timeout
2026-02-15T12:04:07Z elena INFO retrying id=abc-123 backoff=0.8s attempt=2
2026-02-15T12:04:08Z elena INFO request id=abc-123 attempt=2 -> 200 OK
2026-02-15T12:04:08Z elena WARNING duplicate_delivery id=abc-123 consumer=sampleapp tokens_delivered=2
```

sam: Two things to check: (1) ensure `Idempotency-Key` header is attached to the retry attempt (some transports drop custom headers on redirect/reconnect), (2) confirm the async iterator returned by attempt#1 gets cancelled/closed before promise for attempt#2 is piped to the consumer.

ciara: What backoff strategy are you seeing? Could the jitter implementation be resetting and causing immediate retry instead of exponential?

elena: default backoff (exp * jitter). In this run jitter was small so retry came quickly. Not sure that's the root cause — even if backoff is fast the original iterator should be cancelled.

kevin: I'll take this. Plan: add an integration test that simulates 504 then 200 and asserts consumer only receives one stream. I'll also audit the transport layer to verify headers passed on reconnect. If header lost we can make idempotency header sticky at the retry layer.

kevin: Opening a PR now with tests + fix to cancel previous iterator on retry: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4321 (draft).

ciara: Nice. Can you also increment a telemetry counter `duplicate_deliveries.v1` when we detect this so SRE can alert?

kevin: good call, will add a metric and a temporary canary alert.

sam: One more ask: add a short sample-app note in the SDK docs about streaming semantics and recommended idempotency usage for long-lived streams. New users keep getting bitten by this pattern.

elena: thanks — repro + gist here: https://gist.github.com/elena/stream-dup-repro (contains minimal async script). Workaround for now: set server-side dedupe on idempotency key or avoid retrying streaming calls (set `retry=False` for critical streams).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of `kevin/stream-retry-cancel` succeeded in region-us-west-2. Monitoring `duplicate_deliveries.v1` for 30m. :rocket:
